text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak decided to extend to 10 years from five years tax exemption for small projects for young people, financed by the Social Fund.He also cut interest rate on loans extended by the fund to seven from eight percent. This is the second rate cut.
- Pope Shenouda of the Coptic Church calls for a unified Arab stand to face Judaisation measures in Jerusalem.
- Mubarak to discuss with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Israeli settlement and the importance of resuming Israeli-Syrian negotiations.

- Mubarak travels to Paris on Friday to discuss with French President Jacques Chirac obstacles on the path to peace. The two leaders will exchange views on bilateral relations and increasing French investments in Egypt.
- Share prices continue to rise at the stock exchange. The Capital Market Authority's index rose 6.8 points to end at 400.54 points.
- The chairman of the biggest contracting company in Egypt, The Arab Contractors, Ismail Osman, says the company will not be privatised.
- Mubarak receives the first IDcard under a new standardised national system which gives each citizen a single number.
